questions.q: Why does "where's the data?" matter so much when choosing a cloud AI platform?
options: The model should move to the data, not the other way around — moving large datasets across clouds is slow and often expensive
Data location has no real effect on cloud AI platform choice
Only AWS allows data to stay in its original location
Azure requires all data to be deleted before AI processing
questions.explain: Data gravity favors deploying compute near existing data rather than moving large volumes of data to a different cloud.

questions.q: Why does an organization's existing cloud footprint often outweigh a marginally better model on a different cloud?
options: Because existing identity, networking, and billing setup on that cloud has real value that a slightly better model doesn't offset
Because switching clouds is illegal under most software licenses
Because models perform identically on every cloud regardless of platform
Because only one cloud provider is allowed per company
questions.explain: An org's existing identity, networking, and billing integration on a cloud is a real, practical advantage worth more than marginal model improvements elsewhere.

questions.q: What do Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, and Google's Vertex AI/Model Garden have in common underneath their different branding?
options: They are all exactly the same product rebranded three times
A model catalog, plus a managed service that deploys and calls whatever model is chosen from it
They all require the exact same CLI commands
They only work with each vendor's own models, with no third-party options
questions.explain: Despite different names and UIs, all three solve the same underlying problem: a catalog of models, and a managed layer to deploy and call them.

questions.q: According to the lesson's "honest default," when should you reach for a cloud AI platform different from the one your org already uses?
options: Whenever a new model release gets good press coverage
Never — you should always stay on your current cloud no matter what
Only when there's a real reason, like a model genuinely unavailable elsewhere or a data residency requirement the current cloud can't meet
Every quarter, to evaluate new options regardless of need
questions.explain: The honest default favors the cloud an org already runs on, switching only for a concrete, justified reason rather than hype.

questions.q: Why isn't "which cloud has the single best model this month" usually the deciding factor in a real platform choice?
options: Because model quality converges quickly across providers, and most platforms host more than one provider's models anyway
Because model quality is impossible to measure
Because all clouds are contractually required to offer identical models
Because model choice doesn't affect any AI application's output
questions.explain: Since model quality converges across vendors and most platforms host multiple providers, the specific 'best model' factor is less decisive than practical integration factors.
